translations.text: Adam, Seth, Enosh.
Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared.
Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech.
Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Diphar, and Togarmah.
And the sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Doranim.
And the sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
And the sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. And the sons of Raamah: Sheba and Daran.
And Cush fathered Nimrod; he began to be a mighty man on the earth.
And Mizraim fathered Ludim, Yaabim, Lehabim, and Yaphtuhim.
And Pathrusim and Casluhim, from whom came the Philistines and the Cappadocians.
And Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn and the Hittites.
And the Jebusites, the Amorites, and the Girgashites.
And the Hivites, the Arkites, and the Sinites.
And the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites.
The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
And Arphaxad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.
And two sons were born to Eber. The name of one was Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided, and his brother's name was Joktan.
And Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, and Jerah.
And Hadoram, Uzal, and Diklah.
And Obal, Abimael, and Sheba.
And Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah.
Eber, Peleg, Reu.
Serug, Nahor, Terah.
Abram, who is Abraham.
These are the sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael.
These are their descendants: Ishmael’s firstborn, Nebaioth, then Qard, Arbel, and Mibsam.
And Mishma, Rumah, Massa, Hadad, and Tema.
And Natir, Naphish, and Kedemah. These are the sons of Ishmael.
The sons of Keturah, Abraham’s concubine: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. The sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan.
The sons of Midian: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Elraa. All these were the sons of Keturah.
Abraham fathered Isaac. The sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel.
The sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
The sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek.
The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
The sons of Seir: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
The sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam. Lotan’s sister was Timna.
The sons of Shobal: Alian, Manahath, Obal, Shepher, and Avim. The sons of Zibeon: Ana and Anah.
The sons of Anah: Dishon. The sons of Dishon: Hamran, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan. The sons of Dishon: Uz and Aram.
These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before a king reigned over the Israelites: Bela son of Beor reigned in Edom, and the name of his town was Dihab.
Bela died, and Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah reigned after him.
Jobab died, and Husham from the land of the Temanites reigned after him.
Husham died, and Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated the Midianites in the fields of the Moabites, reigned after him. The name of his town was Gavith.
Hadad died, and Samlah from Masrekah reigned after him.
Samlah died, and Shaul from Rehoboth on the River reigned after him.
Saul died, and Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned after him.
Hadad reigned after him. The name of his town was Pau, and his wife’s name was Mehetabel, daughter of Matred son of Mezahab.
Hadad died. These were the chiefs of Edom: Chief Timna, Chief Anah, Chief Jetheth.
Chief Oholibamah, Chief Elah, Chief Pinon.
Chief Kenaz, Chief Teman, Chief Mibzar.
Chief Magdiel, Chief Giram. These are the chiefs of Edom.
These are the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, Asher.
The sons of Judah were Er, Onan, and Shelah. These three were born to him by Bath-shua the Canaanite woman. Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the Lord, and he killed him.
Tamar, his daughter-in-law, bore him Perez and Zerah. Judah had five sons in all.
The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.
The sons of Zerah were Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Darda, five in all.
The son of Carmi was Achar, the troubler of Israel, who acted unfaithfully concerning the things devoted to destruction.
The son of Ethan was Azariah.
The sons born to Hezron were Jerahmeel, Ram, and Salchi.
Ram fathered Amminadab, and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, the leader of the descendants of Judah.
Nahshon fathered Salma, and Salma fathered Boaz.
Boaz fathered Obed, and Obed fathered Jesse.
Jesse fathered Eliab his firstborn, Abinadab the second, and Shammah the third,
Nethanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth,
Ozem the sixth, Elihu the seventh, and David the eighth.
Their two sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. The sons of Zeruiah were Abishai, Joab, and Asahel, three in all.
Abigail bore Amasa, and Amasa’s father was Jether.
Caleb son of Hezron fathered Jerioth by Aruba his wife. These were her sons: Zeker, Asher, Shobab, and Adon.
Aruba died, and Caleb married Ephrath, who bore him Hur.
Hur fathered Uri, and Uri fathered Bezalel.
After this, Hezron slept with the daughter of Machir, the father of Gilead, and married her. He was sixty years old, and she bore him Segub.
Segub fathered Jair, who had twenty-three towns in the land of Gilead.
After this, Hezron died in Caleb’s land, in Ephrath. She had borne him sons: [?], the father of Tekoa.
The sons of Jerahmeel, Hezron’s firstborn, were Aram, Baana, Oren, and Ozem, their sister.
Jerahmeel had another wife named Atarah. She was the mother of Onam.
The sons of Aram, Jerahmeel’s firstborn, were Maaz, Nabin, and Atar.
The sons of Onam were Sabi and Jada. The sons of Sabi were Nadab and Abishur.
Abishur’s wife was named Abihail, and she bore him Ahban and Molid.
The sons of Nadab were Seled and Pelarim. Seled died without children.
The sons of Pelarim were Isaiah; the sons of Isaiah were Sheshan; and the sons of Sheshan were Ahlai.
The sons of Jada, Sabi’s brother, were Jether and Jonathan. Jether died without children.
The sons of Jonathan were Laphath and Zaza. These were the sons of Jerahmeel.
Sheshan had no sons, only daughters. Sheshan had a man from Egypt as a son-in-law, whose name was Jarha.
Sheshan gave him his daughter as a wife, and she bore him Attai.
Attai fathered Nathan, and Nathan fathered Debir.
Debir fathered Aphil, and Aphil fathered Jobab.
Jobab fathered Jehu, and Jehu fathered Azariah.
Azariah fathered Helez, and Helez fathered Eleasah.
Eleasah fathered Samsi, and Samsi fathered Shallum.
Shallum fathered Jekamiah, and Jekamiah fathered Elishama.
The sons of Caleb, Jerahmeel’s brother, were Alhamshi his firstborn, who was the father of Ziph, and the sons of Mareshah, the father of Hebron:
Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
Shema fathered Raham, the father of Jorkeam, and Jorkeam fathered Shammai.
Ephah, Caleb’s concubine, bore Haran, and Haran fathered Gazez.
These were the sons of Caleb son of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah: Shobal was born in Kiriath-nearim.
Salma was born in Bethlehem. Abi was born in Geder.
Shobal had sons in Kiriath-nearim:
Ataroth, Jubal, Hazar-sepharim, Netophath, Salma, Shemuathim, Shecab, and Hamma. All these were Shobal’s sons in Kiriath-nearim.
These were David’s sons in Hebron. His firstborn son was named Amnon, by Ahinoam from Jezreel. The second was Caleb, by Abigail, the wife of Nabal from Mount Carmel.
The third was Absalom, the son of Maacah, daughter of Talmai king of Geshur. The fourth was Adonijah, the son of Haggith.
The fifth was Shephatiah, the son of Abital. The sixth was Ithream, by Eglah, David’s wife.
These six sons were born to David in Hebron. He reigned there for seven years and six months, and he reigned in Jerusalem for thirty-three years.
These are the names of the sons born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shacub, Nathan, and Solomon.
And Ibhar and Elishama.
And Nogah, Nepheg, and Naphia.
And Eliada and Eliphat.
All these were David’s sons, and Tamar was their sister.
And Solomon’s sons: Rehoboam his son, Abijah his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son,
Jehoram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son,
Amaziah his son, Uzziah his son, Jotham his son,
Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,
Amon his son, Josiah his son.
And Josiah’s sons: his firstborn Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, and the fourth Shallum.
And Jehoiakim’s sons: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son.
And Jeconiah’s son: [?], his son.
And Malchum his son, Peraiah his son, Shaazzar his son, Nehemiah his son, Shammua his son, and Nedabiah his son.
And Nedabiah’s sons: Zerubbabel and Shimei. And Zerubbabel’s sons: Meshullam and Hananiah, and Salqath their sister.
And Hashba, Jehuel, Beriah, and Hasadiah.
Hananiah’s sons: Pelatiah and Hoshaiah, Arphaiah his son, Arnan his son, Obadiah his son, the son of Hoshaiah.
And Shecaniah’s son: Shemaiah. And Shemaiah’s son: Hattush and Negael,
and Azariah and Hezekiah.
And Hodiah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Jacob, Johanan, Delaiah, and Ain.
And these were Judah’s sons: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Jaur, and Shobal.
And Laiah son of Shobal fathered Nahath, and Nahath fathered Ahimai, and he fathered these clans of Rehoboam.
And these were Abinadab’s sons: Ahazreel, Nishma, and Dibash,
and Paguael and Hushiah. And these were the sons of Hur, Ephrath’s firstborn, who was a father from Bethlehem.
And Ashhur, the father of Tekoa, had two wives.
And one of them bore Ahiram, Tepher, Teman, and Harshatar. These were the sons of one of them.
And one of them was loved by his mother and his father, and he named him Enai.

And he said to him, “May the Lord indeed bless you and enlarge your territory, and may his hand be with you, and may he deliver you from evil so that it does not gain power over you, and may he give you what you ask of him.”
Caleb, the brother of Ahijah, fathered Mehir, who was the father of Eshton.
Eshton fathered Rapha, Rapha fathered Paseah, Paseah fathered Tehiah, and Tehiah fathered Jaazir. These were the sons of Pallu.

The sons of Caleb son of Jephunneh: the name of his firstborn son was Elah; the name of the second was Naam; the name of the third was Kenaz; the name of the fourth was Ashiph; the name of the fifth was Joel; and the name of the sixth was Jehorub. These were the sons of Caleb son of Jephunneh.
The sons of Huriah’s wife, the sister of Nahum, the father of Keilah: Zimri, Eshtemoa, Makith, Eshtema, and Ishimon.
The sons of Ashimon: Amon, Dumiah, Zerah, and Shelah. These were the sons of Jehudiah, the brother of Nahum, the father of Keilah.
The sons of Shelah son of Judah:
Jemuel, Jamin, Ahar, Jachin, Zohar, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul. These were the sons of Shelah son of Judah.
The sons of Simeon: Mibsam his son, Mishma his son,
Shimeathi his son, Hammuel his son, Zaccai his son, and Shimei his son.
Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, but his brother did not have many sons. All their families did not increase until the descendants of Judah came to him.
They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, and Darath-shua,
in Bilhah, Ezem, and Eltolad,
in Nesel and Hormah,
and in Hazar-gaddah, Heshmon, Hath-pelet, Zangag, Marmana, and Samsala. These were their towns until King David.
And their villages: Aqim, Aqin, Rimmon, Athcan, and Ashan—five towns.

And all the small villages surrounding these towns belonged to the fugitives. These were the towns where they lived. They had a great reputation, their dwelling place was pleasant, and there was quiet and peace around them.
These are the names of the leaders who were there, according to their families and their ancestral houses.
They came to the entrance of Gedor, as far as the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks.
They found good, rich pasture and a broad, good land. There was peace and security there, because those people had lived in it from earlier times.

These men who had been recorded came [?] in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. They destroyed their tents and stopped up all the springs of water there, which remain stopped up to this day. They settled in their place because the pasture for their flocks was very good.

Some of them, five hundred men from the descendants of Simeon, went to Mount Gebal. These are the names of the men who went at their head: Pelatiah, Mattithiah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel. These four men, the sons of Enshai, went at their head.
They destroyed all the remaining Amalekites and settled in their place to this day.

The sons of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn: because he was his father’s firstborn but dishonored his father’s bed, his birthright was given to his brother Joseph, the son of Israel. Upon these two came blessings from all the tribes of Israel.
From Judah will come the Messiah, the king, and the birthright will be given to Joseph.
The sons of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
The sons of Carmi: Shemaiah his son, Doeg his son, and Shimei his son.
Micah his son, Uriah his son, and Bela his son.
Obadiah his son, whom Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria took into exile. He was the chief of the tribe of Reuben.
His brothers, according to their families, when they were listed by their ancestry: their chief was Azriel, and the second was Zechariah.
Bela son of Uzzi, son of Shimei, son of Joel, lived in Aroer, as far as Nebo and the plain of Maon.
To the east he lived as far as the edge of the wilderness extending from the Euphrates River, because they and their livestock had multiplied in the land of Gilead.
In the days of Saul they fought against the Arabs who lived in tents, and these were delivered into their hands. They settled in their tents throughout the eastern part of the land of Gilead.
The descendants of Gad lived opposite them in the land of Bashan, as far as the border of Salba.
Joel went out at their head, judged them, and taught them the Scriptures well.
These were the sons of Abihail son of Hur, son of Zerah, son of Gilead, son of Machir,
son of Abdiel, son of Eli, the heads of their ancestral families.
They lived in Bashan and its villages.
All of them were registered by genealogy in the days of Jotham king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.
The descendants of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh had men who carried swords and shields, shot with bows, and were skilled in warfare: 44,666 men. All these went out to battle.
They fought against the tent dwellers.
These were delivered into their hands because they prayed to the LORD in battle, and he heard their cry because they trusted in him.
They captured much property and livestock: 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, 2,000 donkeys, and 100,000 people.
For many of those from their tents fell slain in battle, and they settled in their place, in their tents.

The members of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land of Bashan as far as the valley of Mount Hermon, as far as Seir, the great mountain of Hermon, and as far as Hartman. They multiplied and became numerous.
These were the heads of their ancestral families: Ephah, Joshab, Eldaah, Azriel, Edomiah, Uriah, and Hazael—mighty warriors, men of renown, who were heads of their ancestral families.
They were unfaithful to the God of their ancestors and went astray after the gods of the peoples of the land whom the LORD had destroyed before them.

The LORD, the God of Israel, stirred up against them the spirit of Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria. He deported the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and brought them to Halah and to Habor, the river of Gozan, in the cities of Media. They live there to this day.
The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The children of Amram: Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Eleazar fathered Phinehas, and Phinehas fathered Abishua.
Abishua fathered Abiqar, and Abiqar fathered Uzzi.
Uzzi fathered Zerahiah, and Zerahiah fathered Meru.
Meru fathered Amariah, and Amariah fathered Ahitub.
Ahitub fathered Zadok, and Zadok fathered Ahimaaz.
Ahimaaz fathered Azariah, and Azariah fathered Johanan.
Johanan fathered Azariah. Azariah was the one who served in the temple that Solomon built in Jerusalem.
Azariah fathered Amariah, and Amariah fathered Ahitub.
Ahitub fathered Zadok, and Zadok fathered Shallum.
Shallum fathered Hilkiah, and Hilkiah fathered Azariah.
Azariah fathered Seraiah, and Seraiah fathered Zadok.
Zadok was taken captive when the Lord sent the people of Judah and Jerusalem into exile in Babylon, to Nebuchadnezzar.
The sons of Levi were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
These are the names of Gershon’s sons: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites according to their ancestral families.
Gershon his son, Nahath his son, and Zimmah his son.
Joah his son, Iddo his son, Zerah his son, and Jeatherai his son.
The sons of Kohath: Amminadab his son, Korah his son, and Assir his son.
Elkanah his son, and Achnasaph his son.
Tahath his son, Uriel his son, Uzziah his son, and Saul his son.
The sons of Elkanah were Amasai and Ahimoth.
Elkanah his son, Zuph his son, Nahath his son, Zerah his son, Shemala his son, and Mari his son.
Eliab his son, Gadhiel his son, and Elkanah his son.
The sons of Samuel, his son: Joel his firstborn, and his second son, whose name was Abijah.
The sons of Merari: Mahli his son, Libni his son, Shimei his son, and Uzza his son.
Shemaiah his son, Hananiah his son, and Asaiah his son.
These are all those whom David appointed to serve in the house of the Lord, in the place where the ark was placed.

They were to serve before the tabernacle, in the tent of meeting, with great songs of praise, until Solomon built the house of the Lord in Jerusalem. He assigned them to their duties according to their regulations.
These were the ministers, they and their sons, from the descendants of Kohath, from the families of the Levites: Heman and Joel son of Samuel,
son of Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Eliel, son of Tohu,
son of Zuph, son of Elkanah, son of Hamath, son of Maasai,
son of Elkanah, son of Joel, son of Azariah, son of Zephaniah,
son of Tahath, son of Assir, son of Achisaph, son of Korah,
son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, son of Israel.
And his brother Asaph, who stood at his right hand: Asaph son of Berechiah, son of Shemaiah,
son of Michael, son of Manassiah, son of Malchiah,
son of Ethni, son of Zerah, son of Ariah,
son of Ethan, son of Zimmah, son of Shimei,
son of Joah, son of Gershon, son of Levi.
From the sons of Merari: their brother Ethan, who was stationed on the left, son of Kishi, son of Omri, son of Malluch,
son of Hashabiah, son of Amaziah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Nattur,
son of Mahli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Levi.
And their fellow Levites, who were assigned to all the duties of the tabernacle of the house of the Lord.

Aaron and his sons made offerings on the altar of burnt offerings and on the altar for burning fragrant incense, attending to all the work of the Most Holy Place, to make atonement for Israel, just as Moses, the servant of the LORD, had commanded.
These were Aaron’s descendants: Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son,
Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son,
Meru his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son,
Zadok his son, Ahimaaz his son.
These are the names of the towns allotted within their territories to the families of Aaron’s descendants, of the family of Kohath, because the first lot fell to them.
They gave them Hebron in the land of Judah and all its surrounding villages in the land of Judah.
All the fields of the towns around it they gave to Caleb son of Jephunneh.
To Aaron’s descendants they gave all the towns of refuge. They gave the priests Hebron and its villages, Libnah and its villages, Jattir and its villages, and Eshtemoa and its villages,
and Lehem and its villages, and Debir and its villages.
And Ashan and its villages, Ether and its villages, and Beth-shemesh and its villages.
From the tribe of Benjamin they gave Geba and its villages, Alemeth and its villages, and Anathoth and its villages: thirteen cities in all for their clans.
To the sons of Kohath who received an inheritance from the tribe of the clan of Manasseh, ten cities in number.
To the sons of Gershon, according to their clans, from the tribe of Issachar, the tribe of Asher, the tribe of Manasseh, and the tribe of Naphtali in Bashan, thirteen cities.
To the sons of Merari, according to their clans, from the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and the tribe of Zebulun, thirteen cities in number.
The Israelites gave these cities and their villages to the Levites.
They gave by lot, from the tribe of Judah, the tribe of Simeon, and the tribe of Benjamin, these cities that they had called by name.
The clans of the sons of Kohath had cities and their territories from the tribe of Ephraim.
They gave them, as cities of refuge, Shechem and its villages in the hill country of the tribe of Ephraim, and Jazer and its villages.
And Beth-horon and its villages.
And Aijalon and its villages, and Gath-rimmon and its villages.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh they gave Anath and its villages, and Ibleam and its villages, to the clan of the sons of Kohath who received an inheritance.
To the sons of Gershon, from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan and its villages, and Ashtaroth and its villages.
From the tribe of Issachar: Rekem and its villages, and Daberath and its villages.
Elam and its villages.
From the tribe of Asher: Mashal and its villages, and Ebron and its villages.
Aqiq and its villages, and Dahab and its villages.
From the tribe of Naphtali: Rekem in Galilee and its villages, Hammon and its villages, and Kiriathaim and its villages.
Those from the tribe of Merari who received an inheritance received, from the tribe of Zebulun, Armoni and its villages, and Tabor and its villages.
Across the Jordan at Jericho, east of the Jordan, from the tribe of Reuben: Bezer in the wilderness and its villages, Mephaath and its villages, and Jahaz and its villages.
Karmoth and its villages, and Maon and its villages.
Ramoth and its villages; Mahlam and its villages.
Jazer and its villages, and Heshbon and its villages.
The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron. These were his four sons.

The sons of Tola: Uzzi, Arpiah, Nuriel, Lahmi, Jibsam, and Samuel, heads of their ancestral house. These sons of Tola were mighty warriors according to their clans. Their number, according to their genealogical records in the days of David, was 22,600.
The sons of Uzer: Izrahan. The sons of Izrahan: Malkiel, Obadiah, Joel, and Anshua—four, all of them heads.
Their clans, according to their ancestral households, numbered thirty-six thousand mighty warriors trained for battle, for they, their wives, and their children had become numerous.
Their relatives, all the clans of the house of Issachar, numbered eighty-seven thousand mighty warriors.
These are the names of the sons of Benjamin: Bela, Achbor, Eshcol, Gera, Naaman, Ahi, Arosh, Muppi and Huppim, and Addar.
The sons of Bela were Ezbon, Uzzi, Zael, Jerimoth, and Ezri: five heads of ancestral households, mighty warriors. Their number was twenty-two thousand and thirty-four.
The sons of Achbor were Zemirah, Jeush, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jerimoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemoth. All these were sons of Achbor.
Their count, according to their clans, the heads of their ancestral households, and their genealogies, was twenty-two thousand two hundred mighty warriors.
These were the sons of Eshcol: Bilhan. The sons of Bilhan were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehur, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahsharah.
All these were sons of Eshcol, according to the heads of their ancestral households and their clans: seventeen thousand two hundred mighty warriors who went out with the army for battle.
Shuppan and Huppis were sons of Gur, sons of Hushiah.
The sons of Naphtali were Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum. These were the sons of Bilhah.
The sons of Manasseh whom his concubine bore him were Isracel and Adomiah. She also bore Machir, the father of Gilead.
Machir took a wife, a daughter of nobles. His sister's name was Maacah, and his older brother's name was Zelophehad. Zelophehad had no sons, only daughters.
Maacah, Machir's mother, also bore him a son and named him Peresh. His brother's name was Sheresh. The sons of Ulam were Rekem.
The sons of Rekem were Beran. These were the sons of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh.
His sister Maacah bore Ishhur and Abiezer,
and Shemariah, Elion, Shim, and Itham.
The sons of Ephraim were Shuthelah, Becher his son, Tahath his son, Eleadah his son, and Ahath his son,
and Zabur his son, Shuthelah his son, and Eleazar his son. Men of Gath who were born in the land had gone down to take their possessions.
Their father Ephraim mourned for many days, and his brothers came to comfort him and speak reassuringly to him.
He went to his wife, and she conceived and bore a son. She named him Beriah because misfortune had come upon her in her household.
And her daughter who remained, Lower and Upper Beth-horon, and all these that remained [?].
Asith his daughter, because she was a physician and treated the sick, and she healed
Ladan son of Ammihud,
one of the sons of Anun, the father of Jehosheba.
Their inheritance and their settlements were Bethel and its villages, Shechem and its villages, and Anath and its villages.

Along the border of the descendants of Manasseh were Beth-shechem and its villages, Taanach and its villages, Megiddo and its villages, and Dor and its villages. In these towns the descendants of Joseph son of Israel settled.
The sons of Asher were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah, and their sister was Serah.
The sons of Beriah were Heber and Malchiel, who was the father of Birzaith.
Hepher fathered Pelet, Shomer, Hotham, and their sister Shua.
The sons of Pelet were Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These were the sons of Pelet.
Arah and Hananel.

All these were descendants of Asher, heads of their ancestral houses in their generations, mighty warriors and leading chiefs. Their number, counted for military service in battle, was twenty-six thousand men.
Benjamin fathered Bela his firstborn, Akbar the second, and Eshcol the third,
Gera the fourth, Naaman the fifth, Ahi the sixth, Rosh the seventh, Muppim the eighth, Huppim the ninth, and Addar the tenth.
Bela's sons were Abdo, Gera, and Abihur,
Abishua, Naaman, and Ahiah,
Shuppim, Huppim, and Ahiram.
These were the sons of Abihur, and these were the heads of their ancestral houses according to their clans. They went into exile to the valley
of Naaman.
By his wife Harash he fathered Jobab, Zibia, and Malcom,
Manasseh, Seraiah, Jermana, and Jizbaz. These were his sons, heads of ancestral houses.
By Hushim he fathered Ahitub and Elipheleg.
The sons of Elipheleg were Obed, Meshullam, and Shomer. He built Ayo and Lod and its villages.
He was the head of the ancestral houses over the inhabitants of Gath.
Shishak and Jeremoth,
Zebadiah, Adru, and Adi,
Mankel and Anshaphai,
Ibron, Zabdi, and Hanin,
Hananiah, Ulam, and Anathoth,
Peraiah and Pael, the sons of Shishak.
And Shemariah.
These were the heads of the ancestral families according to their genealogies, those who formerly lived in Jerusalem.
The father of Gibeon lived in Gibeon, and his wife’s name was Maacah.
And his firstborn son Ebron, and Kish, Bela, and Nadab,
and Gedud, Ahib, and Ibzar,
and Mikloth. Mikloth fathered Maah. They too lived opposite their relatives in Jerusalem.
Ner fathered Kish, Kish fathered Saul, and Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchishua, Ishvi, and Eshbashul.
Jonathan’s son was lame in his feet. Ishvi had a son, Merib-baal, and Merib-baal fathered Micah.
The sons of Micah were Pithon, Immelech, Tada, Ahur, and Aran.
Merib-baal fathered Jehoiada, and Jehoiada fathered Almoth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri fathered Amaziah.
Amaziah fathered Kenaaniah, and Kenaaniah fathered Rapha and Eleasah his son; Azel was his son.
Azel had six sons: Azri his firstborn, Kayyam his second, Ishmael the third, Sheadiah, Obadiah, and Hanan. All these were Azel’s sons.
The sons of his brother Eshek were Ulam his firstborn, Jeush the second, and Eliphelet the third.
Ulam’s sons were mighty warriors who wielded bows and gave instruction. They, their sons, and their grandsons numbered one hundred and fifty. All these belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.
All the Israelites were registered, along with the people of Judah, the evildoers who were exiled to Babylon because of their wickedness.
Those who first settled in their inherited lands and in their towns were the Israelites, the priests, the Levites, and the resident foreigners.
People from the descendants of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh lived in Jerusalem.
Zeuri son of Ammihud, son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Benjamin, from the descendants of Perez, the descendants of Judah.
From the region of the Shilonites: Asaiah his firstborn and Bezaiah his brother.
From the descendants of Zerah: Zeuel and their relatives, six hundred and ninety.
From the descendants of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Hodiah, son of Jahbena,
and Jeconiah son of Jeroham—these were the sons of Uzzi son of Machir—and Meshullam son of Areubel, son of Jeconiah.
Their relatives, according to their clans, numbered nine hundred and ninety-nine. All these were mighty warriors, commanders of hundreds according to their clans.
From the priests: Jonadab, Joiada, Nakim,
Azariah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Maru, son of Ahitub, who lived in his house opposite the house of the Lord,
and Azariah son of Jeroham, son of Pashhur, son of Malchah, and Maasi son of Aduel, son of John, son of Meshullam, son of Meshraoth, son of Immer.
Their relatives, the heads of their ancestral households, numbered one thousand seven hundred and sixty, mighty men who carried out the work of the house of the Lord.
And from the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hashum, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, from the descendants of Merari.
Jeroham son of Hadosh, son of Elal; Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zabdi, son of Asaph;
and Obadiah son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun; and Berechiah son of Asaph, son of Elkanah, who lived in Ramah.
Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Hamnon, Ahihum, and Shallum.
Up to this point, the king's eastern gate. These are the gates at which the guards of the Levites are stationed.

And Shallum son of Kore, son of Ekanasaph, son of Korah, and his relatives and the members of his ancestral household were responsible for the work and guarded the entrance to the tabernacle. Their ancestors were over the camps, and they guarded the exits and entrances.
Phinehas son of Eleazar had been their chief in earlier times, and the Lord was with him.
Zechariah son of Meshelemiah guarded the entrance to the tent of meeting.
All these stationed at the gates numbered 212. They were counted in their divisions. David and Samuel the prophet had appointed them because of their faithfulness.
They appointed these men and their sons to guard these gates of the Lord's house and the house of the tent of meeting, and to keep watch.
These gates opened in the four directions: east, west, north, and south.
Their relatives kept watch in their turns, coming in only once every seven days, from one appointed time to the next.
For these men held positions of trust, since these Levites stood guard at the gates in all four directions. They were responsible for the work and for the treasury of the Lord's house.
They stayed overnight around the Lord's house, because this was their duty of guarding the entrance, and every morning
they inspected all the utensils used in the service, because they brought them in by count and took them out by count.
Some of the Levites were responsible for the utensils and all the sacred work, for the altar, the utensils, the wine, the oil, the frankincense, and the pure spices.
Some of the sons of the priests prepared the aromatic spices for the censers.
A gift was given by the Levites. Mattithiah, one of the Levites, was Shallum's firstborn. He was entrusted with responsibility for the hidden work.
Some of the descendants of Kohath were also responsible for their relatives and for the bread set out in rows, to prepare it every Sabbath.
These attendants, the heads of the Levites' ancestral households, kept watch in the rooms surrounding the house, because they were responsible for the work day and night.
These were the heads of the Levites' ancestral households according to their genealogies, and they lived in Jerusalem.
The father of Gibeon lived in Gibeon. His firstborn son's name was Joel, and his wife's name was Maacah.
And his second son, Abdon, and Zur, Kishon, Baal, Ner, and Nadab.
And Gedud, Ahijah, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
Mikloth was the father of Shimeaz. They too lived opposite their relatives, together with their relatives in Jerusalem.
Ner was the father of Kish, Kish was the father of Saul, and Saul was the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Ishvi [?], and Ishbashul.
Ishvi had a son whose name was Merib-Baal, and Merib-Baal was the father of Micah.
The sons of Micah were Pithon, Ahimelech, and Ahaz.
Ahaz fathered Jaaziah, Jaaziah fathered Alemeth, Alemeth fathered Zimri, and Zimri fathered Moza.
Moza fathered Kenaniah; his son was Rephaiah, his son was Azel, and his son was Eleasah.
Azel had six sons, and these were their names: Azri his firstborn, Kim his second, Ishmael his son, Sheadiah his son, Obadiah his son, and Hanan his son. These were the sons of Azel.
The Philistines were fighting against Israel, and the men of Israel fled from the Philistines. Many fell dead on Mount Gilboa.
The Philistines overtook Saul and his sons, and the Philistines killed Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua, Saul’s sons.
The fighting grew fierce around Saul, and archers who were very skilled at shooting with the bow found him. When Saul saw them, he was greatly afraid of them.

Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and stab me with it before these uncircumcised men come and kill me and abuse me.” But his armor-bearer was unwilling, because he was very afraid. So Saul drew his sword and fell on it.
When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his sword and died with him.
So Saul, his three sons, his armor-bearer, and all his warriors died together that day.

All the people of Israel who were on the other side of the valley and on the other side of the Jordan saw that the people of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons had been killed. They abandoned their towns and fled, and the Philistines came and settled in them.
The next day, the Philistines came to strip the dead and found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.

They took their heads and stripped off their armor, and sent word throughout the land of the Philistines, to the villages, cities, and fortified towns, to announce the good news in the temples of their idols and among their people.
They placed their armor and weapons in the temples of their idols and hung their bodies on the wall of Beth-shan.
The inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul.

All the brave men rose and traveled all night. They took Saul’s body and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth-shan, brought them to Jabesh, and burned them there. They took their bones and buried them under the terebinth tree in Jabesh, and fasted for seven days.
Saul died because he had acted unfaithfully toward the Lord and had not kept what he commanded him. He had also consulted mediums.
He did not consult the Lord his God, and his kingdom was given to David son of Jesse.
All the Israelites gathered around David at Hebron and said to him, “We are your blood and your flesh.

“Even in the past, when Saul was king over us, you were the one who went out and came in at the head of Israel. The Lord said to you, ‘Go, you will shepherd my people Israel, and you will be ruler over all the tribes of Israel.’”

All the tribes of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David swore an oath to them at Hebron before the Lord. They appointed David king over Israel, and the words of Samuel the prophet, which he had spoken in the Lord’s name, were fulfilled.
David and all the Israelites went to Jerusalem, which had formerly been called Jebus. The Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, were there.
The inhabitants of Jebus said to David, “You will not enter here.” But David gathered all the people and captured the towns of Zion. These came to be called the towns of David.

Then David said, “Whoever is the first to kill a Jebusite man will become chief and commander of the army.” Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and King David appointed him chief and commander of the army.
David lived in the towns of Zion; that is why they called them the towns of David.
David built around the city, from the trench outward, and David gave assistance to the rest of the people who were in the towns.
David grew increasingly wealthy, and the mighty Lord was with him.
These were the leaders of David’s warriors who supported him in his kingship, establishing him as king over all Israel, according to the word the Lord had spoken concerning Israel.
This is the list of David’s warriors: the one who occupied the first seat, the chief of the thirty, was Gadino the mighty warrior. He drew his spear and killed eight hundred men at one time.
After him was Eleazar son of Dodo, from the village of Dahuh. He was in command of three hundred men.
He was with David at Pas-dammim, where the Philistines were fighting. There was a field there sown with barley, and the people scattered before the Philistines.
They took their stand in the middle of the field, saved it, and defeated the Philistines. The Lord brought about a great victory.
Three of the warriors went down to David at the cave of Gatam, while the Philistine armies were encamped in the Valley of the Giants.
David was staying in the tent, and the Philistine warriors were in Bethlehem.
David felt a longing and said, “Who will give me water to drink from the great well of Bethlehem, which is at the town gate?”

At that very moment, the three men heard, broke through, and entered the Philistine camps. They went and drew water from the large well in Bethlehem, at the city gate. They took it, brought it, and gave it to David, but he would not drink it. He poured it out before the Lord.
He said, “May the Lord forbid that I should do this before my God! These men went out at the risk of their lives.” He would not drink it. These were the deeds of the three warriors.
Abishai, Joab’s brother, was chief of the thirty. He drew his spear against three hundred men and killed them, and he was held in higher honor than the thirty.
He was more honored than the thirty and became their chief. He fought like thirty men.

Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a mighty warrior from the town of Kabzeel, whose deeds were outstanding. He killed two mighty warriors of Moab. He also went down and killed a lion in a thicket on a snowy day.

He killed an Egyptian, a powerful man five cubits tall. The Egyptian held a spear whose head was as thick as a weaver’s beam. Benaiah went down against him with a staff, took the spear from the Egyptian’s hands, and killed him with that very spear.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada did all these things, and he had a greater reputation than the three warriors.
He was more honored than the three, and he performed [?] like the three. David appointed him keeper of his spear.
And in charge of the mighty warriors: Asahel, Joab’s brother; Elhanan son of Dodo, from Bethlehem;
Shammoth, from the King’s Mountain; Helez, from Palton;
Ira son of Ikkesh, from Tekoa; Abiezer, from Anathoth;
Sibbi, from Hushath; Ilai, from Hoh;
Maharai, from Netophah; Heled son of Baanah, from Netophah;
Ittai son of Ribai, from Gibeah of the Benjaminites; Benaiah son of Pirathon;
Hiddai, from Nahal-gaash; Abiel, from Arabathon;
Uzban, from Marham; Elipha, from Shaalabim;
The sons of Shem from Azzun; Jonathan son of Shage from Mount Carmel.
Ahiram son of Sacam, from Mount Betha; Eliphon son of Addo, from Begratun;
Hepher, from Mecherathim; Ahijah, from Hazor;
Hezrai, from Carmel; Lazarus, from Obed.
Joel, Jonathan’s brother; Mekhad from Gad.
Zelek the Ammonite and Mahzi the Beerothite, the armor-bearers of Joab son of Zeruiah.
Ira from Jattir; Arab from Jether.
Uriah the Hittite; Zabad son of Ahlai.
Gadino son of Shaara, from the tribe of Reuben. He was the head of the tribe of Reuben and commanded thirty men.
Jehoshaphat.
From Ashtaroth; Shama and Amiel, the sons of Hotham from Araroth.
Jediael son of Shimri, and Joha his brother; Amuzoth.
And Anael, Mahavim, Mozil, Ribai and Anshua his son, Ahmiel and Ithmah the Moabite.
Eliel and Ithmah and Obir, Laasael and Ashkir.

All these were David’s mighty warriors who stood with him in battle. These were the men who entered the town of Ziklag with David when he was fleeing from Saul son of Kish. All David’s men stood bravely, and if he had wished, they would have killed Saul son of Kish for him, because they were mighty warriors and men experienced in battle. But David was unwilling to let them kill Saul.
For they held bows in their left hands and swords in their right hands, and their bows were full of arrows. But David did not want to kill Saul—he was the head of the tribe of Benjamin.
These are the names of David’s men who were with him: Ahiezer and Joash his son, and Joel from Meska; Shemaiah from Gibeath; Pelet and Berechiah, the sons of Arubath; Jehu from Anathoth.
Shemaiah from Gibeon was commander over the thirty, and he fought like all of them.
Jeremiah, Nahzael, Zebur, Eder.
Addi, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Uzzi, Shemariah, Shephatiah, Heber.
Elkanah, Josha, Azarel, Shebna, Asaph.
Joah and Zechariah, the sons of Jeroham from Gedor.

From the tribe of Gad, men were chosen for David to go out with him to the strongholds in the wilderness: mighty warriors, men of powerful stature, men strong in [?], carrying swords and shields. Their appearance was like that of lions, and when they fought against a mountain, they uprooted it.
Azariah, the chief of the mighty warriors; Obadiah, the second; Eliab, the third.
Ashu, the fourth; Jeremiah, the fifth.
Attar, the sixth; Eliel, the seventh.
Johanan, the eighth; Elizabar, the ninth.
Makon, the tenth; Shephatiah, the eleventh.
These were descendants of Gad, army commanders, some commanding a hundred men each and others commanding a thousand each.

These were the men who crossed the Jordan in the month of Nisan, when it was full to its banks, and put to flight the whole army that was camped in the plain, to the east and to the west. These are the numbers of the army commanders who came and gathered around David at Hebron to give him Saul’s kingdom, so that the word of Samuel the prophet, which he spoke from the mouth of the Lord, would be fulfilled.
Some of the descendants of Benjamin and Judah came to David at the camp.

David went out to meet them, blessed them, and said to them, “If you have come in peace to help us, may the Lord give you twice what is in your hearts. But if you have come to deceive me and hand me over to my enemies, although I have done you no wrong and there is no evil on my hands, the God of my ancestors knows, and he will rebuke whichever of us wrongs the other.”

A spirit of courage came upon Amasa son of Jether, the leader of the Thirty. He spoke to David and said, “Come, David! Come, son of Jesse! I too am with you. Peace to you; do not be afraid. Peace has been given to you by your helper, for your God is your helper at all times.” David welcomed them, and David appointed them as leaders of the army.

Some from the tribe of Manasseh went with David when he was going to wage war alongside the Philistines. They were unwilling to go into battle with Saul to help him, because they hated him. They had secretly gone and made an agreement with the Philistine rulers, saying to them, “We will go first and attack Saul our master
when he goes to Ziklag. We will encamp against him and capture him alive.” These were their names: Ada, Zabor, Jediael, Mankiel, Elihu, and Jozabar, commanders of thousands from Manasseh.
They went and helped David when he went against the raiding band, because they were all exceptionally strong warriors. They had authority over the entire army and did with it as they wished.
Every day they came before David to eat bread in his presence, because he loved them very much.
The descendants of Judah who carried shields and held spears numbered 6,800, mighty warriors ready for battle.
From the descendants of Simeon there were 7,100 mighty warriors ready for battle.
From the descendants of Levi there were 4,600.
Jehoiada was the leader of Aaron’s clan, and there were 3,700 with him.
There was also Zadok, a young man and a mighty warrior, along with his father’s household and his relatives, twenty-two leaders.
From the descendants of Benjamin, Saul’s relatives, there were 3,000. Until the day Saul was killed, they had guarded Saul’s household.
From the descendants of Ephraim there were 20,800 mighty warriors, men renowned in their clans and ancestral households.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh there were 18,000 men who had been designated by name. They came to be the first to establish David as king.

From the descendants of Issachar there were men who understood the wisdom of their times and did what was good and right before the Lord. Their leaders numbered two hundred, and all their relatives did whatever they told them.
From the tribe of Zebulun, 50,000 mighty warriors went out, fighting wholeheartedly with their weapons to wage war against those who opposed David’s kingship.
From the descendants of Naphtali there were a thousand leaders, accompanied by 37,000 men carrying shields and spears.
From Dan, 28,600 fighting men went out.
From Asher, 40,000 mighty warriors went out to wage war.
From across the Jordan, from the tribe of Reuben, from Gad, and from the half-tribe of Manasseh, there were 120,000 men equipped with their weapons of war.

All these men went down to battle, mighty warriors with steadfast hearts. They came to Hebron to establish David as king over all Israel. All the leaders of Israel also came with steadfast hearts to establish David as king over Israel.
They stayed there with David for three days, eating and drinking, because their relatives had provided them with food.

These are the names of the nearby tribes that brought provisions to them: the tribes of Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali. They brought bread on donkeys, camels, and mules, along with flour, cakes of figs, baskets of grapes, wine, oil, and sheep and cattle in very great numbers, because there was great joy in Israel.
David consulted with the commanders of thousands and hundreds and with all the leaders, administrators, and rulers of Israel.

David said to all the assemblies of Israel, “If it seems good to you, let us ask the LORD our God to repair for us the breaches among our brothers who live in all the towns of Israel. Let us settle priests and Levites with them in their towns and villages, and let them gather and come to us.
Let them pray before the LORD our God, and let us petition him concerning our sins, because we did not pray before him in the days of Saul.”
All the assemblies agreed to do this.
David gathered all Israel, from the river of Egypt to the entrance of Antioch, to bring the ark of the LORD from Kiriath-jearim.

David and all Israel went up to Kiriath-jearim, within the territory of the tribe of Judah, to bring up from there the ark of the LORD God, who sits enthroned above the lofty cherubim, whose name was invoked over it.
He placed the ark of the LORD on a new cart. They took it and came out from Abinadab’s house, while Uzzah and his brother drove the cart.
David and all Israel were praising the LORD with all their might, with songs of praise, harps, lyres, and cymbals.
They came to the threshing floors where heaps lay, and Uzzah reached out his hand to steady the ark, because the oxen were running toward the threshing floors.
The LORD became angry with Uzzah and struck him there because he had reached out his hand toward the ark, and he died there before the ark.
David was distressed because the LORD had broken out against Uzzah. That place has been called “The Breach against Uzzah” to this day.
David was afraid of the LORD that day and said, “How can I bring the ark of the LORD to me?”
David was unwilling to bring the ark of the LORD to himself in the City of David, and David ordered them to take it to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
The ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months, and the LORD blessed the household of Obed-edom the Gittite and everything he had.
Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David. He also sent him cedar timber, builders, and carpenters to build him a house.
Then David knew that the LORD had chosen him to be king over Israel, and that his kingdom had been greatly exalted so that he might be king over his people Israel.
David took wives from Jerusalem after he came from Hebron, and sons and daughters were born to David.
These are the names of the sons born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, [?], Nathan, and Solomon.
And Ibhar, Elishama, and Eliphelet;
and Niah, Nepheg, and Naphia;
and Elishua, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
The Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, and all the Philistines went up to seek David. David heard about it and went out to meet them.
The Philistines came and camped in the Valley of the Giants.
David inquired of the LORD, saying, “Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you deliver them into my hands?” He said to him, “Go up, and I will deliver them into your hands.”

They went up to the Plain of the Breach, and he defeated them there. David said, “The LORD has broken through my enemies before me like water breaking through.” Therefore they called that place the Plain of the Breach.
They left their idols there, and David said to his warriors, “Burn them in the fire and scatter their ashes in the wind.”
The Philistines came up again and camped in the Plain of the Giants.
David again inquired of the LORD, and he said to him, “Do not go up. Instead, turn away from them, and go meet them from the front.”
When you hear the sound of wailing on the mountaintop, then go out to battle, because then the Lord will go out before you to destroy the Philistine camps.
David did as the Lord had commanded him, and he destroyed the Philistine camp from Gibeon as far as Gaza.
David went out to all the cities, and the Lord made all the peoples fear him.
He built palaces for himself in the towns of David, and he built a place for the ark of the Lord and for the furnishings of the tabernacle.

Then David told the Levites to carry the ark of the Lord and the furnishings of the tabernacle, because the Lord had chosen the Levites to minister, to carry the ark of the Lord, and to serve him forever.
David gathered all Israel in Jerusalem to bring the ark of the Lord up to the place he had built for it.
David gathered the descendants of Aaron and the Levites.
He spoke to them and to the descendants of Kohath—to Uriel the elder and his 120 relatives.
For the descendants of Merari: Asahel the chief and his relatives, two hundred and twenty.
For the descendants of Gershon: Joel the elder and his 130 relatives.
For the descendants of Elizaphan: Shemaiah the elder and his 200 relatives.
For the descendants of Hebron: Eliab the elder and his eighty relatives.
For the descendants of Uzziel: Amminadab the chief and his relatives, one hundred and twelve.
David summoned Zadok the priest, Abiathar, the Levites, Uriel, Laasa, Oiel, Asaiah, Isaiah, Uriel, and Amminadab.

He said to them, “You are the heads of the ancestral families of the Levites. Consecrate yourselves, you and your relatives, so that you may bring the ark of the Lord, the God of Israel, up to the place that was built for it beforehand,
so that the Lord our God will not break out against us, because we did not seek him according to the prescribed rule.”
The priests and Levites consecrated themselves to bring up the ark of the Lord, the God of Israel.
The Levites carried the ark of the LORD, as Moses had commanded according to the word of the LORD; they carried it on their shoulders.

David told the elders of the Levites to appoint their relatives who ministered and offered praise with musical instruments—with harps, lyres, and cymbals—to make themselves heard, raising their voices joyfully.
The Levites appointed Heman son of Joel; from his relatives, Asaph son of Berechiah; and from the descendants of Merari, their relatives, Ethan son of Kushaiah.
With them were their relative of the second rank, Zechariah son of Neiel, and Jehiel, Eliab, Benaiah, Asa, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel. All these stood guard at the gates.
Heman, Asaph, and Ethan offered praise; all these offered praise in their ministry with songs of praise on bronze instruments.
Azariah, Azael, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah, and those who offered praise with songs of praise.
Mattithiah, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Uzziel, and Uzziah—these ministered with lyres every day, at the third, sixth, and ninth hours.
Benaiah, the chief of the Levites, carried it every day in the shelter, because a place had been prepared for him.
Berechiah and Elkanah attended to whatever the ark needed.
Shebna, Jehoshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer were the priests who sounded the horns before the ark of the Lord. Obed-edom and Ahijah attended to the ark.
David, the elders of Israel, and the commanders of thousands went with great joy to bring the ark of the covenant of the Lord up from the house of Obed-edom to the city of David.
When the Lord helped the Levites who were carrying the ark containing the covenant of the Lord, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
David was dressed in fine linen garments, and all the Levites carrying the ark were also dressed in fine linen garments. Over his fine linen garments, David wore a fine linen ephod.
David and all the house of Israel were bringing up the ark containing the covenant of the Lord, with songs of praise and the sound of straight and curved horns, raising their voices to heaven.

When the ark containing the covenant of the Lord arrived and entered its place in the City of David, Michal, Saul’s daughter, looked out through the window. She saw King David rejoicing and dancing, and she despised him in her heart.
They brought in the ark of the Lord and placed it in its place inside the tent that David had pitched for it. They offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the ark of the Lord.
When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people of Israel in the name of the mighty Lord.

He distributed to all the people, to all the house of Israel, from men to women and from soldiers to nursing infants, one loaf of bread, one portion, and one [?] for each person. Then all the people went home, each to their own house.
He appointed Levites to serve before the Lord, to commemorate, give thanks, and praise the Lord, the God of Israel.
Asaph was their chief, Zechariah was second, then Joel, Johael, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Asaph, Amminadab, Asaph, Nehazael, and Asaph.
All these were priests who sounded the horns continually before the ark of the Lord.

Then on that day David opened his mouth, together with the heads of all the priests and Levites, to praise the Lord with the choir of Asaph and his brothers. These are the opening lines of the songs of praise that David recited before the ark of the Lord on that day.
Give thanks to the LORD and call on his name; make his deeds known among the nations.
Praise him and give thanks to him; recount all his mighty deeds.
Glory in his holy name; let the hearts of all who seek the LORD rejoice.
Seek the Lord and his strength; pray before him continually.
Remember the mighty deeds he has done, his mighty deeds and the judgment of his mouth.
You descendants of Abraham his servant, you children of Jacob, the chosen ones whom he chose.
He is the Lord our God; his laws are throughout the whole earth.
Remember his covenant forever, the word he commanded for a thousand generations,
which he swore to Abraham, and the covenant he gave to the children of Isaac.
He established it for Jacob forever, and he gave Israel a covenant forever and ever.
He said to them, “To you I give the land of Canaan as your allotted inheritance.”
When you were few in number, a small group living in it,
and you were taken captive from nation to nation and from one kingdom to another,
he did not allow rulers to oppress you, and he rebuked kings for your sake.
He said to them, “Do not touch my anointed ones, and do not harm my prophets.”
Praise the Lord, all the earth; proclaim his salvation day after day.
Recount his glory among the nations.
For the Lord is great and greatly praised; he is feared above all the nations.
For all the idols of the nations are images, but the Lord made the heavens.
Praise and splendor are before him; strength and greatness are in his sanctuary.
Give praise to the LORD, families of the nations; give praise before the LORD for his glory and strength.
Give thanks to the Lord in honor of his name. Bring offerings and give thanks before him with the prayer of your mouths. Worship the Lord with praises of his holiness.
Let the whole earth tremble before him. Let the world be firmly established so that it cannot be shaken.
Let the heavens rejoice and the earth give praise. Let them say among the nations, “The Lord reigns!”
Let the sea and everything in it give praise. Let the fields and everything in them rejoice.
Then the trees of the forest will give praise before the Lord, who comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness and rebuke the nations with faithfulness.
And he said, “Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, and his kindness lasts forever.
Save me, Lord, save me! Gather us and bring us near from among the nations, so that we may give thanks to your holy name and praise you with your praises.
Blessed is the Lord of lords of Israel, from eternity to eternity.” Let all the people say, “Amen!” With a pleasant and pure mouth, let them praise their God.
He left Asaph and his relatives there before the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to serve continually before the LORD, each on his appointed day.
Obed-Edom and his brothers numbered sixty-eight. The younger Obed-Edom, son of Jartom, and Hosah—all these were gatekeepers at the outer gates.
Hezron the priest and his fellow priests—all these were priests serving before the Lord’s tabernacle at the great altar in the town of Gibeon,

to offer burnt offerings to the Lord on the altar of burnt offering continually, morning and evening, and to do everything written in the law of the Lord, which he gave through Moses to teach the Israelites.

These are the names of the men appointed to lead the praises: Heman, Arithun, and the rest of the righteous men whose names were concealed, to give thanks to the Lord because his kindness lasts forever.

These righteous men gave praise, not with musical instruments, nor with [?], nor with [?], nor with curved horns, nor with straight ones, nor did they give praise with cymbals. Instead, with a pleasant mouth, with pure and perfect prayer, with righteousness and integrity, they praised the Lord, the mighty God, the Lord of Israel, the Lord of all deeds.
David dismissed the people, and everyone went home. David returned to his own home to bless his household.
While David was living in his house, he said to Nathan the prophet, “Look, I live in a house roofed with cedar beams, while the ark of the Lord stays inside a tent made of hair.”
Nathan said to David, “Go and do everything you have in mind, for the Lord is with you.”
That night the word of the Lord came to Nathan the prophet, and he said to him,
“Go and tell my servant David: This is what the Lord says: You will not build me a house to live in.
For I have not lived in a house from the day I brought Israel up from the land of Egypt until today. Instead, I have moved from tent to tent.

Throughout all the time I traveled among all the Israelites, did I ever say a word to any of the judges of Israel whom I appointed to judge my people Israel, asking them, ‘Why have you not built me a house roofed with cedar?’
Now tell my servant David: This is what the mighty Lord says: I took you from the sheepfold, from following the sheep, to be king over my people Israel.
I have been with you everywhere you went. I destroyed all your enemies before you and made your name great, like the names of the great ones on earth.

I will establish a place for my people Israel and settle them there. They will live in their own place and will no longer be disturbed. Wicked people will no longer drive them into exile as they did before.
From the day I made you judge over my people Israel, I have given you rest from all your enemies. The Lord has shown you that your kingdom is established for you forever.
When the days of your life are complete and you go to be gathered to your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring after you, one who comes from your own body, and I will establish his kingdom.
He will build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me. My kindness will not depart from him as I took it away from Saul, who was before you.
I will give him authority over my house and my kingdom forever and ever, and the throne of his kingdom will be established for him forever.
Nathan the prophet spoke to David in accordance with all these words and this entire vision.
King David came and sat before the Lord and said, “Who am I in your sight, Lord of lords, and what is my household, that you have brought me this far?

Yet this was a small thing in your eyes, Lord of lords, for you have spoken about your servant’s household far into the future. You bring out of darkness into light all people who worship you with their whole hearts, Lord of lords.
What more can your servant David boast of saying before you? Your servant’s deeds are known to you, Lord of lords.
Because you know what is in your servant’s heart, you have done all these great things for him, making them known to your servant.
Therefore I know, Lord of lords, that there is no one like you, and there is no God except you, according to everything we have heard with our own ears.

Who is like your people Israel, a unique people on earth? You revealed yourself from heaven and redeemed them. For their sake you brought great and terrifying trials and great plagues upon the Egyptians, until you brought them out from among them.
You established your people Israel for yourself, to be your people forever and ever, and you, Lord, became their God.
Now, Lord, establish forever the word you spoke concerning your servant and the members of his household, and do as you have said.

May your deeds be confirmed forever, and may your name be praised throughout the world. May people say, ‘The mighty Lord, the Lord of lords, is the God of Israel.’ May the household of your servant David be established before you forever.
For you, my God, revealed a secret to your servant and said to him, ‘Build me a house.’ Therefore your servant resolved in his heart to pray this prayer before you.
Now, Lord, you are my God, and all your words are true. The things you have spoken to your servant are good.

Now reveal yourself to bless your servant’s household, so that it may remain before you forever and ever. For you, Lord, Lord of lords, have spoken, and through your blessing the households of the righteous are blessed forever.”

After these things, David defeated the Philistines and destroyed them. David took the measuring line from the Philistines’ control, and he took Gath and its small surrounding villages from the Philistines.
He defeated the Moabites, and the Moabites became subjects who paid tribute.
David killed Hadadezer king of Nisibis when he went to establish a boundary at the Euphrates River.
David captured from him a thousand teams of horses and seven thousand horsemen. David hamstrung all the teams of horses but spared a hundred teams.
The men of Edom and Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Nisibis, and David killed twenty-two thousand men from Edom.
David appointed governors in Damascus, and the people of Damascus became David’s subjects and paid tribute. The Lord delivered David wherever he went.
David took the gold shields that hung on the horses of Hadadezer’s servants.

From Tebah and Berothai, towns belonging to Hadadezer, David took a very large quantity of bronze. From it David made the bronze Sea, bronze pillars, bronze oxen, and a very large number of bronze utensils.
Pul king of Antioch heard that David had defeated the armies of Hadadezer king of Nisibis.

He sent his son Joram to King David to ask about his welfare and congratulate him because he had fought against Hadadezer and killed him, for Hadadezer was a warlike man. Joram brought articles of silver, gold, and bronze.

King David also dedicated these to the Lord, together with the silver and gold he had taken from all the nations he had conquered: the Edomites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Philistines, and the Amalekites.
Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, struck down eighteen thousand Edomite men in the Valley of Salt.
David appointed governors over the Edomites, and all the Edomites became David’s subjects. The Lord delivered David wherever he went.
David reigned over all Israel, administering justice and righteousness for all the people.
Joab son of Zeruiah commanded all the armies, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder.
Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests, and Seraiah was the scribe.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was in charge of the archers and slingers, and David’s sons were high officials.
After these things, Nahash king of the Ammonites died, and his son Hanun reigned in his place.

David said, “I will certainly show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, just as his father showed kindness to me.” David sent messengers to console him over his father. David’s servants came to Hanun in the land of the Ammonites to console him.

The Ammonite officials said to their lord Hanun, “Did David really honor your father during his lifetime, that he has now sent you men to console you? David has sent his servants to us to spy out the city and learn its exits and entrances.”
Hanun seized David’s servants, shaved off half their beards and the hair on half their heads, cut their tunics up to their buttocks, and sent them away.
David was told, and he sent men to meet them, because they were deeply ashamed. The king told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back, and then return.”
The Ammonites realized that they had wronged David’s servants. Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariot teams and horsemen from Mesopotamia, Haran, Nisibis, and Edom.

They hired thirty-two thousand horsemen, along with the king of Haran, the king of Edom, the king of Aram-naharaim, the king of Nisibis, and their armies. They came and camped before Medeba. The Ammonites gathered from their towns and came to battle.
David heard about it and sent Joab and all the forces of mighty warriors.
The Ammonites came out and drew up for battle in front of the gate, while those kings and their armies were encamped separately in the fields.
Joab saw that the battle pressed hard against him from both the front and the rear. He selected for himself [?] from all the mighty warriors of Israel, and they drew up for battle against Edom.
He entrusted the rest of the troops to his brother Abishai, who drew them up against the Ammonites.
He said to him, “If Edom proves too strong for me, come and rescue me. If the Ammonites prove too strong for you, I will come and rescue you from them.”
“Be strong and take courage! Let us fight for our people and for the towns of our God. May the Lord do what is good in his sight.”
Joab and the troops with him advanced to fight the Edomites, and they fled before him.
When the Ammonites saw that the Edomites had fled, they too fled before his brother Abishai and entered the city. Joab returned to Jerusalem.

The Edomites saw that they had been defeated by the Israelites. They sent messengers and brought out the Edomites who were beyond the River. They came to Helam, with Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer’s army, leading them.
David was informed, and he gathered all Israel and came against them. David drew up his forces for battle against the Edomites, and they fought against them.
The Edomites fled before the Israelites. David destroyed seven thousand Edomite chariot teams and killed four thousand foot soldiers. Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer’s army, was killed there.
Hadadezer’s servants saw that they had been defeated by the Israelites, so they made peace with David and served him. The Edomites were unwilling to help the Ammonites again.

The following year, at the time when kings go out to war, Joab gathered the armies, came and encamped in the land of the Ammonites, and took possession of it. He besieged Rabbah, their great city, while David remained in Jerusalem. Joab captured Rabbah, their city, and demolished it.

David took their king’s crown from his head and weighed it. He found that it weighed a talent of gold, and it contained fine gems. David put it on his own head. He also brought out a very great amount of plunder from the city.

He brought out the people who were in it and bound them with chains, iron collars, shackles, and fetters. He bound them all. He did the same to all the people found in the towns of the Ammonites, but he did not kill any of them. He went and settled them in the towns of the land of Israel. Then David and everyone with him returned to Jerusalem.
After these things, there was another battle with the Philistines at Gaza. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Sippai, who was one of the descendants of the reviling clan.
He was the brother of Goliath, the mighty warrior from Gath, and the head of his spear was as thick as a weaver’s beam.
There was another battle at Gath. There was a mighty warrior there, a man of great size, who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in all. He too was born to taunt.
He taunted Israel, and Jonathan son of Shammah, David’s brother, killed him.
These four were born in Gath to taunt, and they were struck down by David and his servants.
Satan rose up against Israel and urged David to count Israel.
David said to Joab son of Zeruiah and to the leaders of the people, “Go and count the people of Israel from Beersheba to Dan. Then come back to me so that I may know the number of the people.”

Joab said to King David, “May the LORD your God increase his people a hundredfold, and may the eyes of my lord the king see it, for they are all his servants. But why has our lord the king taken pleasure in this matter?”
But the king’s command prevailed over Joab. So Joab went out, traveled throughout Israel, and returned to Jerusalem.

Joab gave David the number and total of the people. The total for the Israelites was 1,100,000 foot soldiers who could draw the sword, and the tribe of Judah numbered 470,000 men who could draw the sword.
The Levites, the priests, and the tribe of Benjamin were not counted with them, because Joab despised the king’s command and did not want to count them.
This matter was displeasing in the LORD’s eyes, because David had counted Israel.
David said to the LORD, “I have sinned greatly in what I have done in this matter. Now take away your servant’s sins, for I have acted very foolishly.”
David rose early in the morning, and the word of the LORD came to Gad the prophet, saying to him:
“Go and tell David, ‘This is what the LORD says: I am bringing three calamities upon you. Choose one of them for yourself, and I will bring it upon you.’”
Gad the prophet came to David and said to him, “This is what the LORD says: Accept for yourself

either three years of famine in your land, or three months of being handed over to your enemy, with him pursuing you and having power over you, or three days of the LORD’s sword in Israel. Now consider and decide what answer you will give to the one who sent me to you.”
David said to Gad, “I am in great distress. Let us fall into the hands of the LORD, for his mercies are very great, but let us not fall into human hands.”
The LORD sent a plague upon Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.

The LORD sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it. As he was destroying it, the LORD saw him and relented concerning the calamity. He said to the destroying angel, “You have destroyed enough. Now withdraw your hand.” The angel of the LORD was stationed beside the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

David looked up and saw the angel of the LORD standing between heaven and earth, holding his drawn sword in his hand and standing above Jerusalem. David fell down, and the elders who were with him were clothed in sackcloth, and they fell on their faces.

David said to the LORD, “I was the one who ordered the people to be counted. I am the one who sinned, and the folly I committed was very great. But these innocent sheep—what have they done? LORD my God, let your hand be against me and my father’s household, and let the plague be stopped among the people.”
The angel of the LORD said to Gad the prophet, “Go up and tell David, ‘Go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.’”
David went up according to the word of Gad, who had spoken in the name of the Lord.
David saw that the angel who was destroying the people had drawn back his hand and was no longer destroying them.
David came to Ornan. Ornan turned, saw King David, and bowed before David with his face to the ground. Then Ornan came out of his threshing floor.

David said to Ornan, “Give me the site of this threshing floor so that I may build an altar to the Lord on it. Give it to me for money at a fair price, so that the plague may be stopped among the people.”

Ornan said to David, “Take it for yourself, my lord the king, and let my lord the king do whatever seems good to him. I will give the oxen for the burnt offering, the threshing sledge for firewood, and the wheat for the grain offering. I will give everything that is needed.”
King David said to Ornan, “Certainly not! I will buy it from you for money at its full value, because I will not take what is yours and offer the Lord a burnt offering that costs me nothing.”
David bought that threshing-floor site from Ornan for fifty staters.

David built an altar to the Lord there and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings of lambs. He prayed before the Lord, and he answered him. Fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offerings that were on the altar.
When he saw this, the Lord said to the angel, “Return your sword to its sheath.”
At that time, when David saw that the Lord had answered him at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he offered great sacrifices there.
He prayed there before the tabernacle that Moses had made in the wilderness when the Israelites came out of Egypt.
At that time David was very afraid and could not go to pray before the Lord, because he was afraid of the sword of the angel of the Lord.
David said, “This is the house of the Lord God, and this is the altar for Israel’s burnt offerings.”
David ordered all the foreigners living in the land of Israel to be gathered, and some of them to be made stonecutters to cut stones for the house of the Lord.
He also ordered some of them to be made smiths, workers in iron, to make nails, [?], and iron fittings. David prepared these, along with so much bronze that it could not be weighed.
There were also countless cedar timbers, because the people of Tyre and Sidon brought David cedar timber in great abundance.

David said, “My son Solomon is still a young boy, and it is about him that it is said in the writing that he will build a house for the Lord, to exalt it above all others in renown, greatness, and praise throughout all the cities. During my lifetime I will prepare everything he needs.” So David prepared everything needed for the house, and nothing was lacking.
He called his son Solomon and said to him, “You are to build a house for the Lord God, the Lord of lords of Israel.

For he sent word to me through the prophet and said to me, ‘You have shed much blood and fought great battles. You must not build a house for my name, because you have shed much blood on the earth before me.

But the son who will be born to you will be a man of rest. I will give him rest from all his enemies around him. His name will be Solomon, and there will be peace and rest throughout all Israel in his days.
He will build a house for my name. He will be like a son to me, and I will be like a father to him. I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever and ever.’
And now, my son, may the LORD be with you, and may you succeed and build the house of the LORD your God, as he told you.
He will give you wisdom and prophecy and appoint you over Israel, and you are to keep the laws of the Lord your God, just as he commanded me.

Then you will succeed, if you observe and carry out these commandments, laws, and judgments, just as the Lord commanded Moses to teach Israel. So be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or terrified.

Look, I have prepared everything for you, everything needed for building the house of the Lord. I have prepared for you a hundred thousand talents of gold. I have prepared for you a million talents of silver. I have prepared for you bronze and iron beyond counting. No one who walks the earth can calculate their total weight in pounds, because there is so much. I have also prepared timber and stones for you, and you are to add to them.
Increase the number of workers: stonecutters, builders, and carpenters,
and workers in gold, silver, bronze, and iron, beyond counting. Be steadfast and get to work, and may the Lord be your help.”
David commanded all the elders of Israel and told them, “Help my son Solomon.”

For the LORD your God is with you, helping you and supporting you against all those around you. He has handed over to you all the inhabitants of the land, and the land will be subdued before the LORD and before his people.

“And now prepare your hearts and souls to pray before the Lord your God. Get up and build the sanctuary of the Lord God, and bring there the ark in which the covenant of the Lord our God is placed, along with the sacred utensils of the Lord our God. Build a house for his great name, which has been invoked over us.”
David grew old and full of days, and he appointed his son Solomon as king over Israel.
He gathered all the elders of the priests and the Levites.
The Levites thirty years old and upward were counted, and the number of men, counted individually, was thirty-eight thousand.

From among them David appointed supervisors over the work of the Lord’s house, twenty-four men over each thousand, and judges and scribes, six men over each hundred. They were to oversee the construction, attend to their responsibilities, and exert themselves in their activities, their work, their accounts, their property, and the charitable giving by which they were to provide for the poor. David appointed providers and caretakers over the poor and those in distress, one over every ten, to feed and provide for the poor and let them lack nothing.
