David appointed them all to their positions of authority—the descendants of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
To Gershon belonged Ladan and Shimei.
The sons of Ladan: Nahnael, the eldest, Jotham, and Joel—three.
The sons of Shemaiah: Shelomoth, Hazael, and Aran—three. These were the heads of the ancestral households of Shimei.
The sons of Shimei: Nahath, Zabida, Jeush, and Beriah. These were the four sons of Shimei.
Nahath was the eldest, and Zabida the second, and Jeush and Beriah. Beriah did not have many sons, and they formed one clan in their ancestral household.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel—four.

The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. Aaron was chosen, he and his sons forever, to serve in the Holy of Holies, to offer fragrant incense before the Lord, to serve him, and to bless in his name forever.
Moses, the prophet of the Lord, was reckoned as belonging to the tribe of the house of Levi.
The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
The sons of Gershom: Samuel, his eldest.
The sons of Eliezer were Rahmiah, his eldest. Eliezer had no other sons. The sons of Rahmiah: Ribbi, his eldest.
The sons of Izhar: Shelomoth, his eldest.
The sons of Hebron: Judah, the eldest, Amariah the second, Nahaziel the third, and Nekamaim the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel: Micah, the eldest, and Shuah the second.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
Eleazar died without sons, having only daughters, and the sons of Kish, their uncle, married them.
The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jarmun—three.

These were the descendants of Levi according to their ancestral households, the heads of ancestral households as they were counted, with their names recorded individually, those twenty years old and upward who were responsible for the work required in the Lord’s house.
For David said, “The Lord of lords has given rest to Israel his people, and he dwells in Jerusalem from now and forever.”
Those Levites are also to carry the tabernacle and all the equipment used for its service.
For according to David’s final instructions, the census of the descendants of Levi was completed, counting those twenty years old and upward.

For he appointed them alongside Aaron’s descendants to have authority in the house of the Lord over those who sound the straight and curved horns, and over the storerooms where the Lord’s sacred utensils are kept.
And for the bread of the Presence, the fine flour, the unleavened cakes, and all those who offer praise and thanksgiving.
They were to stand every morning to thank and praise the Lord, and likewise every evening.
They were also to offer burnt offerings to the Lord on the Sabbaths, at the new moons, and at the festivals, in the numbers required of them, continually before the Lord.

They were to take care of the tabernacle’s equipment and the sacred utensils, and to carry out the duties assigned by their relatives, Aaron’s descendants, whenever they were required to serve in the house of the Lord.
As for Aaron’s sons, these were their divisions. Aaron’s sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died during the lifetime of their father Aaron, and they had no sons. Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
David, together with Zadok from Eleazar’s descendants and Ahimelech from Ithamar’s descendants, divided them according to their numbers and their responsibilities.

Eleazar’s descendants were found to have more heads of families than Ithamar’s descendants. He divided them according to the heads of their ancestral families: Eleazar’s descendants numbered sixteen, and Ithamar’s descendants numbered eight.
He divided them by lot, one group along with the other, because sanctuary leaders and priestly authorities came from both Eleazar’s descendants and Ithamar’s descendants.

Shemaiah son of Methlael, a scribe from the Levites, recorded them before King David, the elders of Israel, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the heads of the ancestral families of the priests and Levites. The first ancestral family was one from Eleazar, and the next was one from Ithamar.
The first lot fell to Jehoiada, and the second to Jedaiah.
The third to Hadam, and the fourth to Seorim.
The fifth to Malchijah, and the sixth to Mamin.
The seventh to Hakkoz, and the eighth to Abijah.
The ninth to Elisha, and the tenth to Shecaniah.
The eleventh to Elisha, and the twelfth to Eliakib.
The thirteenth to Huppah, and the fourteenth to Hadiah.
The fifteenth to Bilgah, and the sixteenth to Immer.
The seventeenth to Ahaziah, and the eighteenth to Pazzin.
The nineteenth to Pethahiah, and the twentieth to Ezekiel.
The twenty-first to Nekannam, and the twenty-second to Gamul.
The twenty-third to Delaiah, and the twenty-fourth to Maadiah.

These were their appointed divisions for their duties, entering the house of the Lord according to their regulations, as required of them under the direction of Aaron their father, just as the Lord of lords of Israel had commanded.
As for the remaining sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shobal; of the sons of Shobal, Jehdeiah.
And Rehabiah; of the sons of Rehabiah, Shua, his eldest.
And Izhar and Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Nahath.
And Jeremiah, Hazael, and Nekameam.
The sons of Hazael: Micah. For the sons of Micah: Shamir.
And Jeshua; of the sons of Jeshua, Zechariah.
The sons of Uzzim: his son.
These are the sons of Levi, according to their ancestral houses.

They too cast lots alongside their brothers and the sons of Aaron, before King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the priests and Levites. In the reckoning and numbering, the younger was counted just like his older brother.
This was the number of the men who carried out the work in their assigned duties.
The sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Israel. These sons of Asaph were the ones whom the king appointed.

For Jeduthun, in songs of praise: the sons of Jeduthun were Azariah, Isaiah, Hashabiah, Mattithiah, and Jeduthun—six. These were entrusted to Jeduthun their father, and they praised with lyres and gave thanks to the Lord.
And from the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shobal, Jeremoth, and Hananiah.
Their number included their brothers, and they sang songs of praise to the Lord. The number of these singers was two hundred and eighty-eight.
The younger was counted just like the older, and the pupil just like the teacher.
The first lot fell to Asaph, to Joseph; the second to Gedaliah—he, his brothers, and his sons, twelve.
The third to Zeuri—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The fourth to Nizri—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The fifth to Nethaniah—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The sixth to Bukkiah—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The seventh to Sariel—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The eighth to Isaiah—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The ninth to Mattaniah—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The tenth to Shimeali—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The eleventh to Uzziel—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The twelfth: Hashabiah, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The thirteenth: Shubael, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The fourteenth: Mattithiah, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The fifteenth: Jeremoth, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The sixteenth: Hananiah, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The seventeenth: Eliashib, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The eighteenth: Hanani, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The nineteenth: Mallothi, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The twentieth: Eliab, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The twenty-first: Jether, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The twenty-second: Jarib, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The division of the gates for which King David appointed guards: Meshelemiah, from the descendants of Joseph.
Meshalliah had seven sons: Zechariah his firstborn, Jediael the second, Zechariah the third, and Nethanel the fourth.
Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Jedai the seventh.
Obed-edom had sons: Shemaiah his firstborn, Jehozaban the second, Joah the third, Sheber the fourth, Matlal the fifth,
Gammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peullethai the eighth, for the Lord had blessed him.
His son Shemaiah also had sons who ruled over their ancestral household, for they were mighty warriors.
The sons of Shemaiah: Gathiel, Gedahiel, Obediel, and Zechariah, mighty warriors; Eliah and Semachiah.
All these were descendants of Obed-edom. They, their sons, and their relatives were mighty men, capable of the work of the sanctuary—sixty-two descendants of Obed-edom.
Meshelemiah, his eldest son, had eighteen sons who were mighty warriors.
Hosah, from the descendants of Merari, had sons who were mighty warriors. His eldest son had died, and his father appointed the next son as chief, but did not give him the title of firstborn.
Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth. All the sons and brothers of Hosah were thirteen.
The gates were assigned to these men, each man with his guard duty alongside their brothers, to serve in the sanctuary.
They cast lots, the small as well as the great, according to their ancestral households, for each gate.
The lot for the east fell to Shelemiah. They cast lots for his son Zechariah, a counselor with understanding, and his lot came out for the north.
To Obed-edom fell the south, and to his sons the house of the thresholds.
To Shuppim and Hosah fell the west, as far as the gate situated on the ascending road, guard post opposite guard post.
On the east, six Levites; on the east, four each day; on the south, four each day; and at the storehouse, two.
At Parbar on the west, four at the roads and two at Parbar.
These were the divisions of the gatekeepers from the descendants of Korah and the descendants of Merari.
Among the Levites, Ahijah was in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the sacred things.
The descendants of Ladan, from the descendants of Gershon belonging to Ladan—the heads of ancestral families belonging to Ladan the Gershonite—were Nahli.
The sons of Nahli, Zetham and his brother Joel, were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the Lord.
As for the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites:
Samuel son of Gershon, son of Moses, was appointed over the treasuries.
As for his brother Eliezer: Rehabiah was his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zichri his son, and Shelomith his son.

This Shelomith and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries of the sacred things dedicated by King David, the heads of ancestral families, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the army commanders.
From warfare and from plunder they dedicated things to strengthen the house of the Lord.
Everything dedicated by Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah—everything anyone dedicated—was entrusted to Shelomith and his brothers.
Among the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were assigned to duties outside the temple, serving as officials and judges over Israel.
Among the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, 1,700 capable men, were responsible for the census of Israel beyond the Jordan to the west, for all the work of the Lord and the service of the king.

Among the Hebronites, Neriah was the head of the Hebronites according to their genealogies and ancestral families. In the fortieth year of David's reign, a search was made, and mighty warriors were found among them at Jazer in Gilead.

His brothers, capable men who were heads of ancestral families, numbered 2,700. King David put them in charge of the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, for every matter concerning God and every matter concerning the king.

The Israelites, according to their numbers—the heads of ancestral families, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and their officials—served the king in every matter concerning the divisions that came on duty and went off duty month by month throughout all the months of the year. Each division numbered 24,000.
Over the first division, for the first month, was Jashobeam son of Zabdiel. His division numbered 24,000.
He was one of the descendants of Perez and was chief of all the army commanders for the first month.
Over the division for the second month was David the Hohite and his division, with Mikloth as the leader. His division numbered 24,000.
The third army commander, for the third month, was Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the chief priest. His division numbered 24,000.
This Benaiah was a warrior among the Thirty and was in command of the Thirty. His son Mizbar was over his division.
The fourth, for the fourth month, was Asahel the brother of Joab, and his son Zabdiel succeeded him. His division numbered 24,000.
The fifth, for the fifth month, was the commander Shamhuth the Nazrahite. His division numbered 24,000.
The sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite. His division numbered 24,000.
The seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, from the descendants of Ephraim. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, from the family of Zerah. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, from the family of Benjamin. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai the Netophathite, from the family of Zerah. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah the Pirathonite, from the descendants of Ephraim. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, from the family of Anthoniel [?]. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Over the tribes of Israel: the leader of the Reubenites was Eliezer son of Zichri; over the Simeonites was Shephatiah son of Maacah.
For Levi: Hashabiah son of Mekuel. For Aaron: Zadok.
For Judah: Elihu, one of David’s brothers. For Issachar: Omri son of Michael.
Over Zebulun was Shemaiah son of Obadiah; over Naphtali was Jeremoth son of Azriel.
Over the descendants of Ephraim was Hoshea son of Azariah; over the half-tribe of Manasseh was Joel son of Periah.
Over the half of Manasseh in Gilead was Iddo son of Zechariah; over Benjamin was Jaasiel son of Abner.
Over Dan was Azriel son of Jeroham. These were the leaders of the tribes of Israel.
David did not count those twenty years old and younger, because the LORD had said that he would make Israel as numerous as the stars in heaven.
Joab son of Zeruiah began to count them but did not finish. Because of this, wrath came upon Israel, and the number was not entered in the account of the chronicles of King David.
Azmaveth son of Adiel was in charge of the king’s treasuries. Jonathan son of Uzziah was in charge of the storehouses in the countryside, in the towns, villages, and towers.
Ezri son of Chelub was in charge of the workers who worked in the fields, cultivating the land.
Shemaiah the Ramathite was in charge of the vineyards. Zabdi the Shiphmite was in charge of the produce of the vineyards for the wine stores.
Over the olive trees and sycamore trees in the lowland: Baal-hanan the Gederite. Over the stores of oil: Jeush.
Shitrai the Sharonite was in charge of the cattle grazing in Sharon. Shaphat son of Adlai was in charge of the cattle in the valley.
Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels. Judah the Meronothite was in charge of the donkeys.
Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of the flocks. All these were the officials in charge of King David’s property.
Jonathan, David’s dear friend, was a counselor, a wise man and a scribe. Jehiel son of Hachmoni was with the king’s sons.
Ahithophel was the king’s counselor, and Hushai the Archite was the king’s friend.
After Ahithophel came Jehoiada son of Benaiah and Abiathar. Joab was commander of the king’s army.

David assembled all the leaders of Israel: the tribal leaders, the commanders of the divisions serving the king, the king’s commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, those in charge of the property and livestock of the king and his sons, the trusted attendants, and the mighty warriors. They all came to Jerusalem.

He said to them, “Listen to me, my brothers and my people. I had it in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the LORD and for the dwelling place of our God. I had prepared everything for building the house.
But the LORD said to me, ‘You shall not build a house for my name, because you are a man of war and because you are a man who has shed much blood.’

Yet the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me from my father’s entire household to be king over Israel forever. For he chose a king for himself from the house of Judah, and from the clan of the house of Judah he chose my father’s household. From my father’s household he chose me to be king over Israel.
Of all my sons—for the Lord has given me many sons—he chose my son Solomon to sit on the throne of the exalted kingdom of Israel.
He said to me, “Your son Solomon will build my house and my courtyards, because I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.”
“I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever, if he does not wish to keep my commandments and my judgments as he does today.”

Now, in the sight of all Israel, the Lord’s people, and before the Lord our God, keep and seek out his commandments. Then you will possess this land forever and ever and pass it on to your children forever and ever, and it will not be ruined.

And you, Solomon my son, know everything that the Lord our God has commanded us, and serve him wholeheartedly and willingly, without compulsion. For the Lord knows everything in the heart and understands everything that people think in their minds. If you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you abandon him, he will destroy you.
Know and see that the Lord has chosen you to build a house for the Lord’s holy name. Be strong, be courageous, and do the work.

David gave his son Solomon the plan of the porches, the measurements of the house, of the [?], of the upper rooms, of the inner colonnades and the outer colonnades, of the upper and lower rooms, of the treasury, of the service room of the Lord’s house, of the slaughtering room, of the room for drinks, and of the room for the lampstands—the place where the gold lampstands were set, with their gold lamps, their lights, their ornaments, and their oil vessels. David wrote everything down and gave it to his son Solomon: silver tables and gold tables, silver pitchers and gold pitchers, [?], forks, and silver strainers. The weight of the gold in these vessels was beyond counting.

David said to his son Solomon, “Be strong, be courageous, and do the work. Do not be afraid or dismayed, because the Lord of lords is with you. He will not let you down or abandon you until you have finished building everything for the Lord’s house.”

Here are the divisions of the priests and Levites. I have put them in charge of all the work of the Lord’s house, and they are with you. They have authority over all the work of Gershon the treasurer, and they carry it out skillfully—all the tasks required for the work of the Lord’s house. I have appointed officials and leaders over them to attend to and carry out all the required tasks.

King David said to all the assemblies of Israel, “This son of mine, Solomon, is a young boy. The Lord chose him from all my sons because he is a wise and discerning boy. This work entrusted to him is not small; it is great, because it has not been entrusted to a mere human being in this way. Be strong and courageous in it, because it belongs to the Lord our God.”

With all my strength and all my possessions, I have prepared everything needed for the house of the Lord my God: gold for the gold work, silver for the silver work, bronze for the bronze work, iron for the ironwork, wood for the woodwork, cedar for the cedar work, precious stones, and pearls.
Everything needed for the house I have prepared and made ready out of my poverty. Out of my poverty I have also prepared money for the expenses of the house of my God.
A million talents of gold, from fine gold, and two million talents of silver, to cover the walls of the house.

Where gold is needed, let gold be supplied; where silver is needed, let silver be supplied, and likewise for all the work, so that the work may be completed in its month. The work must not be delayed, but must be completed as its plan requires.
The heads of the ancestral families, the leaders of the tribes of Israel, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and those in charge of the king’s work gathered together.

They gave for the work of the Lord’s house five thousand talents of gold; fine tin for the pipes, two hundred thousand; twenty thousand talents of silver; seventy thousand talents of Corinthian bronze; and a hundred thousand talents of iron.
They gave silver and gold, as much as was needed, into the treasury of the Lord’s house through Gershon the treasurer.
All the people of Israel rejoiced over all the gifts, because David had given them wholeheartedly before the Lord. David too rejoiced greatly and offered great praises to the Lord.
David blessed the Lord before all the assemblies of Israel. David said, “Blessed are you, Lord, God of our father Israel, from everlasting to everlasting.”

For yours, Lord, are greatness, might, praise, beauty, splendor and honor, because you rule in heaven and on earth. Yours, Lord, is the kingdom, and you rule over everything, and wisdom and might and knowledge.
Wealth and honor come from you, and you rule over everything. Power and might belong to you, and you make great and strengthen all the creatures you have created.
Now, Lord our God, we give thanks to you and praise your great name.
For what am I, and what are my people? For I have learned from all my teachers. Because your way is the way of life, you have helped me, and you are our hope, Lord our God.

For we are like the flame of a cooking pot, and we are sojourners before you, insignificant in the world. You ruled over our ancestors in former times and commanded them which way they should go and live.
We praise you, Lord our God, so that you may deliver us from all who fight against us and insult us—the nations who say to us, “Where is your God whom you serve?”

I know, my God, that you examine the heart and delight in faithfulness. In the faithfulness of my heart I have praised all these things. Now I have also seen your people who are here praising you with great joy and saying:

“Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, our ancestors, keep forever all these things that you promised us. Turn our hearts away from evil so that we do not sin before you, and prepare our hearts to fear you.” I, David, answered and spoke in this way.

Lord my God, give my son Solomon a whole heart to keep your commandments, your testimonies, and your covenant, to do everything you have commanded, and to build the house for which I have made preparations, so that your great name may be held holy and praised in the world you created, before those who fear you.

David said to all the people of Israel, “Bless the Lord your God.” All the people blessed the Lord, the God of their ancestors. They fell down and worshiped the Lord, and they also blessed King David.

They offered sacrifices before the Lord and presented burnt offerings before the Lord on the day after that day: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs, with abundant drink offerings. The Israelites also offered many sacrifices for themselves, in great abundance.
They ate and drank before the Lord that day with great joy. They made Solomon son of David king, and they appointed Zadok as priest.
Solomon sat on the throne of the Lord’s kingdom to reign in place of his father David. He prospered, and all Israel obeyed him.
All the mighty warriors and all the sons of King David submitted to Solomon his son.
The Lord exalted Solomon greatly in the sight of all Israel and bestowed on him royal splendor unlike that of any of the kings of Israel who had preceded him.
David son of Jesse established Solomon his son as king over all Israel.
David reigned over all Israel for forty years. He reigned in Hebron for seven years, and in Jerusalem he reigned for thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.
David son of Jesse died at a good old age, old and satisfied with the days of his life, having grown great in worldly wealth and honor. His son Solomon reigned after him.
The acts of David king of Israel, from first to last, are written in the accounts of Samuel the prophet, in the accounts of Nathan the prophet, and in the accounts of Gad the prophet:

his entire reign, his mighty deeds, and the times that passed over him, over Israel, and over the whole kingdom of his land. For David did what was right before the Lord and did not depart from anything he commanded him all the days of his life.
